shorts.hook: Lake Natron supposedly turns any animal that touches it into stone.
shorts.title: Lake Natron's Stone Animals Were Posed by a Photographer
shorts.outro: Nine other places were less forgiving. The full trip is linked below.
shorts.end_card: WHERE DID DOUG DIE? TAP BELOW
shorts.description: Lake Natron's salty, caustic water really does preserve dead birds and bats, but the famous lifelike poses were arranged by photographer Nick Brandt, so Doug puts on a flamingo costume and finds out what the lake actually does.

shorts.hook: Morecambe Bay looks like England's biggest, flattest beach.
shorts.title: Quicksand Can't Swallow You, but the Tide Will
shorts.outro: And it only gets faster from here. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Physicists found you only sink to your waist in quicksand, but pulling a leg free takes the force of lifting a small car, which matters a lot when Doug is stuck in Morecambe Bay and the tide is coming in.

shorts.hook: Lake Maracaibo gets more lightning than anywhere else on Earth.
shorts.title: Lightning Is Five Times Hotter Than the Sun's Surface
shorts.outro: The next place was not so forgiving. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Lake Maracaibo gets more lightning than anywhere else on Earth, each bolt heats the air to about 50,000 degrees Fahrenheit, and Doug goes night fishing there anyway to test the fact that almost 90 percent of people struck survive.
